policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the verb as the finite second-person clause 'Thou seest many things,' distinguishing the ketiv ראית from the qere infinitive רָאוֹת.

ASV's 'for a spoil' is compatible with both candidate forms; the only note is classed alternative_rendering and therefore does not decide the textual reading. The documented qere base remains the fallback.
